title: Why Power Platform Is Your Real Automation Layer — Not Custom Code
description:
In many Dynamics 365 projects, every automation request ends up as custom code in a developer backlog, and the business pays for it every time a rule changes. This episode shows Dynamics and Power Platform teams where plug-ins still belong, how to make automation visible and owned, and how to migrate safely to Power Platform as the real automation layer.
In this episode
00:00 – Automation as a development backlog04:25 – The hidden cost of custom code08:40 – Where custom code still belongs12:14 – Reasoning between event and action16:46 – Sales approval without a plug-in24:06 – Ownership, solutions and environments35:20 – Governance, DLP and Dataverse security51:09 – Inventory, migration and a 90-day reset
Key takeaways
Keep plug-ins narrow for transactional validation and performance-critical work, and move orchestration across people, systems and time into Power Platform.Business-critical flows need organizational identities, solutions with environment variables and managed deployments instead of personal ownership and production edits.Governance through environments, DLP policies and Dataverse security is an operating model that lets automation scale, starting with an inventory rather than a rewrite.
Worth quoting
“This isn't an argument against developers, it's an argument against using developers as the routing layer for every business process change.” – Mirko Peters (03:36)
“Then somebody asks why dynamics feels slow to change. Dynamics isn't slow, the automation model is.” – Mirko Peters (06:24)
